chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the indication to the صاحب of this matter, so he said:

The indication to him is seniority, merit, and the bequest. When the riders come to al-Madīnah and say, ‘To whom did so-and-so bequeath?’ it is said, ‘To so-and-so son of so-and-so’; and go around with the weapon wherever it goes.
As for the questions, there is no proof in them.

key_terms.الدَّلَالَةِ: the identifying proof or indication by which the rightful Imam is known
key_terms.السِّلَاحِ: the weapon, presented here as a transmitted sign of authority
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: distinction and excellence in virtue and rank
key_terms.الْكِبَرُ: seniority or being the elder as a sign mentioned in context
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: the bequest or explicit designation of succession
key_terms.صَاحِبِ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the holder of this matter, meaning the one vested with the authority of Imamate

ai.seo_question: How is the rightful Imam identified according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains recognized indicators for identifying the rightful Imam, namely seniority, merit, and explicit designation through bequest. It also points to inherited signs of authority, while clarifying that mere questioning by itself is not a decisive proof of the Imam's status.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ahmad Bin Umar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the evidence upon the owner of this matter (Imamate)’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The evidence upon him<sup>asws</sup> is being the elder, and the merit, and the bequest.

When the riders of Al-Medina proceed and they say, ‘To whom has so and so (Imam<sup>asws</sup>) bequeathed to?’ It can be said, ‘To so and so, son of so and so’, and it (the Imamate) would circle around along with the weapons wherever they may be.
So as for the asking questions, so there is no proof in it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar who has said that he asked the following from abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.),
“What is the proof that establishes one’s possessing Divine authority or the his ownership of leadership?”

Such proofs are being the elder, possession of superior moral achievements and one being appointed as the executor of the will. So much so that people would come to the town and ask who is appointed as the executor of the will of so and so it would be said to them so and so son of so and so and these go along wherever the Armament would go.
Asking questions does not establish any authority.”
